stem:
Mona shades a unit square. She takes $\frac{1}{2}$ of the square and then $\frac{1}{3}$ of that half to show $\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{3}$.

Which reading of the shaded product is correct?

options.text: Call the rectangle area the product label, without linking it to the shaded fraction of the unit square.
Shade $\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{3}$ even if the whole region is not the unit square.
The shaded piece is $\frac{1}{6}$ of the unit square, because one half of one third (or one third of one half) is one sixth.
Use the same shading story to find the perimeter of the unit square.

teacher.key_rationale: On a unit square, the product $\frac{1}{2}\times\frac{1}{3}$ is the shaded area $\frac{1}{6}$ of that whole. Relabelling without the unit whole, dropping the unit-square whole, or switching to perimeter all miss that area model.
